answer: Standing is earned by elapsed work, not declared keys: each epoch the chain lights a fresh lantern — an unforeseeable public beacon — and every identity must fold it into its own walnut-hard hash chain through a strictly sequential proof that parallel processors cannot shorten. Miss one horizon and the chain resets to genesis, wiping all accrued age. So a sybil farmer holding M keys needs M always-on rigs grinding the same serial clock, and any merged, replayed, or late chain forfeits its history outright. The toll is relentless wall-clock silicon, never a cheap signature.
